query:
REQUIRED FIRST PANEL ROUND — owner correction, not commands to execute. Owner says in order: “the seed is the lbacking . by adding the btrfs as a device to acieve the rw”; “that is haow it worked before”; “enphasooze that to the panel”; “specy the command btrfs device add”. Explicit mechanism: btrfs device add <writable-device> <mounted-seed-path>. The immutable seed supplies backing; writable member gives the sprout persistent writes. Parent withdraws implication each Incus-exposed subvolume must itself be a block-device operand. Separate seed backing, writable member, Cozo association, exposed subvolumes and separate upgrade replica. NO HOST LOOP DEVICES including pool loops and seed wrappers. Prefer no images/subvolumes only IF all retained semantics survive. No source/runtime/storage/identity/grant/service mutations, provisioning, builds, tests or deployment. No copied-root, snapshot or OverlayFS writable-upper substitution. No new LVM management or VM conversion. JEV is evidence/decision judge, not routing.
ORIGINAL implementation evidence: commit 26a4ad132fbbd4523b05724060bfdeb9ca661824, deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/op-identity-root lines1172–1196:
1172 mount -t btrfs -o "ro,subvolid=5,device=$seed_view" "$seed_view" "$seed_dir/volume"
1173 # Validate the inherited siblings before creating the sprout. Nothing is
1174 # copied or snapshotted; all writes after ADD_DEV go to this new leaf.
1175 initial_members=$(seed_layout_pins) || seed_fail "seed lacks seven distinct sibling subvolumes"
1176 initial_image=$(seed_image_metadata verify) || seed_fail "seed image verification failed before device add"
1177 seed_write --argjson image "$initial_image" '.image=$image'
1178 [ "$(btrfs property get -ts "$seed_dir/volume/@" ro)" = ro=false ] || seed_fail "seed @ must be a normal writable subvolume"
1179 [ -d "$seed_dir/volume/@/etc" ] && [ ! -L "$seed_dir/volume/@/etc" ] || seed_fail "seed root lacks safe etc directory"
1180 seed_write --argjson members "$initial_members" '.members=$members'
1181 current_seed_super=$(btrfs inspect-internal dump-super "$seed_device")
1182 [ "$(blockdev --getro "$seed_device")" = 1 ] || seed_fail "physical seed lost block read-only enforcement"
1183 printf '%s\n' "$current_seed_super" | grep -q SEEDING &&
1184 [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$current_seed_super" | awk '$1 == "fsid" {print $2; exit}')" = "$source_fsid" ] &&
1185 [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$current_seed_super" | awk '$1 == "generation" {print $2; exit}')" = "$source_generation" ] || seed_fail "seed changed before sprout creation"
1186 seed_no_direct_mount
1187 seed_write '.phase="device-add-intent"'
1188 btrfs device add "$leaf_loop" "$seed_dir/volume"
1189 sync -f "$seed_dir/volume"
1190 umount "$seed_dir/volume"
1191 sprout_fsid=$(seed_super "$leaf")
1192 valid_session "$sprout_fsid" && [ "$sprout_fsid" != "$source_fsid" ] || seed_fail "invalid new sprout FSID"
1193 seed_write --arg fsid "$sprout_fsid" '.sprout_fsid=$fsid | .phase="layout-intent"'
1194 mount -t btrfs -o "rw,subvolid=5,device=$seed_view,device=$leaf_loop" "$leaf_loop" "$seed_dir/volume"
1195 seed_verify_volume
1196 [ "$(seed_layout_pins | jq -cS .)" = "$(printf '%s\n' "$initial_members" | jq -cS .)" ] || seed_fail "inherited sibling identities changed after sprout creation"
Hermes ORIGINAL records: id4095 user: "no the persistent cozo iws addedwith btrfs add disk". id4099 assistant: "Right—the persistent writable storage is added to the seed with btrfs device add, and Cozo tracks the identity’s leaf assignment. It is not a writable OverlayFS upper layer. The separate upgrade partition supplies upgrade/@ for the read-only overlay. I conflated those two roles." id4111 assistant: "Yes—the script uses btrfs device add to attach the persistent root partition to the seed, then mounts that pair read-write. prepare-instance-disk.sh:111 — adds the root partition. prepare-instance-disk.sh:116–118 — formats the separate upgrade partition and creates @. bind-instance-root.sh:216 — combines upgrade and seed layers into a read-only overlay. But the storage path is still wrong: the script requires /var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool, rather than your selected /var/lib/incus/storage-pools/3tched-pool. The layout is implemented; that integration is not finished."
Required response: name btrfs device add; identify what the old script added and where, distinguish backing/member from exposed subvolumes and Cozo tracking, trace remount, distinguish script from assistant claims and historical loops from proposed no-loop changes. Reopen conclusions based on layer conflation without inventing replacement topology. State precise unknowns, do not turn operand typing into blanket rejection. Preserve actual successful/failed member identities and exact evidence each received; do not claim consensus from one model. This panel sees only these excerpts, not full histories.

responses.content:
## Decision

Preserve the demonstrated seed/sprout mechanism:

```sh
btrfs device add <writable-device> <mounted-seed-path>
```

Explanatory syntax only; no execution authorized. Reject the earlier inference that every Incus-exposed subvolume must itself be a block-device operand. That conflates filesystem exposure with backing storage and does not establish that the complete arrangement is infeasible.

## What the original script establishes

At commit `26a4ad132fbbd4523b05724060bfdeb9ca661824`, `deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/op-identity-root:1172–1196`:

1. **Mount existing seed backing:** line1172 mounts `$seed_view` read-only at `$seed_dir/volume`, selecting `subvolid=5`.
2. **Check immutable backing and inherited layout:** lines1175–1185 validate seven distinct sibling subvolumes, image metadata, physical seed block read-only status, `SEEDING`, source FSID and generation.
   - Line1178 requires the inherited `@` subvolume’s `ro` property to be `false`. This is not inconsistent with a read-only seed device/mount: those are distinct layers.
3. **Record establishment intent:** line1187 records `device-add-intent`.
4. **Add the writable member:** line1188 executes:
   ```sh
   btrfs device add "$leaf_loop" "$seed_dir/volume"
   ```
   The actual operand shown is **`$leaf_loop`**, added to the filesystem mounted at **`$seed_dir/volume`**—not an exposed subvolume path, Cozo record, or OverlayFS upper directory.
5. **Transition to the sprout:** lines1189–1193 sync, unmount, obtain a sprout FSID from `$leaf`, require it to differ from the source FSID, and record `layout-intent`.
6. **Mount the established pair read-write:** line1194 mounts `$leaf_loop` at the same location with both `$seed_view` and `$leaf_loop` supplied as devices.
7. **Verify preservation:** lines1195–1196 verify the volume and require the inherited sibling identities to match their pre-add values.

This is concrete implementation evidence for the mechanism the owner describes. It is **not an execution receipt proving that this particular invocation completed**.

## Layers that must remain separate

| Layer | Evidence-supported interpretation |
|---|---|
| Immutable seed backing | Supplies the existing filesystem contents; the excerpt checks block read-only enforcement and seed identity. |
| Writable member | `$leaf_loop` is added to the mounted seed to establish the sprout’s writable storage. Its underlying allocation is outside this excerpt. |
| Cozo association | Hermes4099 says Cozo tracks the identity’s leaf assignment. The excerpt does not show the database association, adoption transaction, or recovery lookup. Cozo tracking is not a kernel device. |
| Exposed subvolumes | Seven inherited sibling identities are checked before and after establishment. These are filesystem objects, not necessarily device-add operands. Their exact Incus exposure is not shown. |
| Separate upgrade replica | Hermes4099/4111 describe a separate upgrade partition and `upgrade/@` used in read-only root composition. Those statements need the cited scripts for implementation verification; they do not describe the persistent writable member as an OverlayFS upper. |

Hermes4111’s description of `prepare-instance-disk.sh:111` adding a **root partition** is an assistant claim about another script. It must not be silently substituted for the directly observed `$leaf_loop` operand in `op-identity-root:1188`.

## Revised feasibility finding

**Withdraw any overall-layout rejection derived solely from “a subvolume is not a block device.”** That operand constraint does not determine how seed backing, writable members, Incus volumes and exposed subvolumes can be integrated.

Conversely, this excerpt does **not** prove a compliant no-loop implementation:

- The historical add/remount sequence explicitly references `$leaf_loop`.
- Construction of `$leaf_loop` and `$seed_view` is not supplied here.
- Historical loops cannot be retained under the latest **no host loop devices** rule, including pool backing and seed wrappers.
- Removing loops requires an evidence-backed account of the actual backing and writable-member resources. Renaming fields, recording them in Cozo, or declaring an Incus disk does not supply that account.
- Subvolume-only/no-image operation remains a preference to evaluate against every retained semantic—not a proven replacement topology.

The owner-confirmed previously working mechanism is the baseline to trace, not a reason to invent a replacement or dismiss the arrangement.

## Required continuation

Use the existing checkpointed evidence to resolve these precise unknowns:

1. Trace `$leaf`, `$leaf_loop`, `$seed_device` and `$seed_view` construction, including which historical mapping represented the persistent root partition.
2. Trace identity → Cozo assignment → native UUID → storage proofs → final adoption, distinguishing intent records from successful authoritative receipts.
3. Trace subsequent restoration of the established sprout without repeating device-add during start, stop, login or recovery.
4. Inspect the cited upgrade and binding implementations to establish receive destination proofs, pairing, read-only composition and stopped-state updates.
5. Identify supported no-loop backing/member primitives in the actual existing workflow. Preserve immutable seed dependence, isolated persistent writes and the separate upgrade replica. Do not invent physical allocations or claim native YAML alone implements them.
6. Revise diagnosis and drift findings that relied on layer conflation; retain independently evidenced integration defects and historical failures.

## Panel coverage receipt

- **Evidence received:** the supplied owner correction; the quoted commit/path lines1172–1196; Hermes records4095,4099,4111; and the explicit current constraints.
- **Not independently reviewed:** full histories, surrounding scripts, recovery files, current source, installed helpers, native configuration or runtime receipts.
- **Member identity:** this response is from one advisory panel member; a resolved provider/model identifier was not supplied to this member.
- **Other member outcomes:** unavailable here. No consensus or successful/failed-member count asserted.
- **JEV:** no judgment obtained or represented by this response.
- **Actions:** no tools executed, files written, or system changes made.

consensus: Both responses explicitly acknowledge btrfs device add <writable-device> <mounted-seed-path> as the seed/sprout mechanism to preserve.

Both identify the historical command at line 1188 as adding $leaf_loop to the filesystem mounted at $seed_dir/volume, followed by a read-write mount at line 1194 naming both $seed_view and $leaf_loop.
Both distinguish immutable seed backing, writable membership, exposed filesystem subvolumes and Cozo tracking; Cozo metadata is not itself a kernel block device.
Both reject substituting an OverlayFS writable upper or copied root for the demonstrated persistent writable member.
Both recognize that historical loop use does not satisfy the current prohibition on all host loop devices and that a compliant integration remains unresolved.
Both treat JEV as an evidence/decision judge rather than a model router. Neither supplies an actual JEV judgment.

stances.stance: Explicitly limits its review to supplied excerpts and states that full histories, recovery files, current source, installed helpers and runtime receipts were not independently reviewed.

Lists manifests, constraint files and complete conversation exports as files_read without any supporting tool receipts. These claims exceed the explicitly excerpt-only panel context and cannot count as ingestion.
Withdraws the blanket infeasibility inference but leaves the replacement backing/member topology unproven; construction of $leaf_loop and $seed_view is outside the excerpt.

Declares the mechanism feasible and says the operand must be a native block device or Incus-managed volume. The latter alternative is insufficiently qualified: managed-volume status alone does not establish block-device suitability, and the supplied evidence does not prove a compliant complete topology.

partial_coverage.point: Distinguishes directly quoted script implementation from Hermes4111's claim about a different script adding a root partition. Qwen cites both but does not preserve this evidentiary distinction explicitly.

Explicitly separates the upgrade replica and read-only root composition from persistent writable membership, while marking the upgrade implementation as requiring inspection of the cited scripts. Qwen's layer inventory omits the separate upgrade replica.

Covers durable device-add/layout intents, sync and unmount, distinct sprout FSID validation, and preservation of sibling identities. Qwen traces the main add/remount sequence but omits several of these preservation and recovery checks.

Names subsequent restoration without lifecycle device-add churn, final authoritative adoption and receive/root-binding proofs as unfinished tracing work. Qwen concentrates on operand availability and Cozo fields.

Neither establishes actual resolved provider identities or failed-member coverage. Astra explicitly disclaims that visibility; Qwen provides no member-coverage accounting. The two supplied response labels establish only which responses were presented for comparison.

unique_insights.insight: The inherited @ subvolume having ro=false is distinct from the physical seed device and seed mount being read-only; those observations are not inherently contradictory.
The historical code demonstrates an implemented sequence, not an execution receipt proving that a particular invocation completed.
Comparing seed_layout_pins before and after sprout creation explicitly checks preservation of inherited sibling identities, rather than merely checking that directories exist.

blind_spots: The supplied excerpt does not show how $leaf, $leaf_loop, $seed_device or $seed_view are constructed. Their exact backing and mapping require surrounding source evidence.

Neither response establishes a supported no-host-loop, preferably no-image topology preserving all seed, persistence, upgrade and isolation semantics. Withdrawing the layer-conflation argument does not establish that topology.
The actual Cozo association, native UUID binding, authoritative adoption transaction and recovery lookup are not demonstrated by these excerpts.
The separate upgrade receive/pairing and root-composition implementations remain supported here by assistant statements, not their original source excerpts or execution receipts.
No complete semantic history review, source-versus-installed comparison, current provisioning completion or runtime readiness is established by either response.
Qwen's timestamp and files_read inventory lack observed provenance; its suggested Cozo fields and the underlying file/image construction of $leaf_loop must not be promoted to verified facts.
Neither response provides a persisted panel receipt or actual JEV result. Those deliverables require outer-runner evidence, not inference from panel prose.
